questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Choose tools and an order of work suited to a cleaning job.
questions.prompt: A classroom shelf is dusty and there is dry dust on the tiled floor below it. Which order avoids dropping dust onto a floor that has just been cleaned?
options: Mop the floor, then dust the shelf.
Dust the shelf, then sweep and mop the floor.
Sweep the floor and dust the shelf afterwards.
Mop the floor and move the dust from the shelf to the floor.
questions.answer: Dust the shelf, then sweep and mop the floor.
questions.explanation: Dusting the shelf first lets the group remove any fallen dust while cleaning the floor.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Choose tools and an order of work suited to a cleaning job.
questions.prompt: After sweeping the classroom, pupils find dried mud stuck to a small patch of the washable tile floor. Which tool is most suitable for loosening the mud?
options: A dry feather duster.
A dustpan by itself.
A damp scrubbing brush.
A clean dry chalkboard eraser.
questions.explanation: A damp brush can loosen dirt stuck to washable tile. A dustpan collects loose dirt.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Choose tools and an order of work suited to a cleaning job.
questions.prompt: A group has one cloth for desks and one for the waste-bin lid. Why should they keep the cloths separate?
options: To avoid carrying dirt from the bin to the desks.
To make the desks dry more slowly.
To make the bin hold more waste.
To stop the lid from opening.
questions.answer: To avoid carrying dirt from the bin to the desks.
questions.explanation: Keeping cleaning cloths separate limits the transfer of dirt from a dirtier surface to a cleaner one.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select meals or menu descriptions that meet stated needs and constraints.
questions.prompt: A school lunch plan already includes rice. The teacher asks pupils to add a pulse and a leafy vegetable. Which pair meets both requests?
options: Yam and plantain.
Chicken and bread.
Beans and fish.
Beans and ugu leaves.
questions.explanation: Beans are pulses. Ugu is a leafy vegetable.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select meals or menu descriptions that meet stated needs and constraints.
questions.prompt: The cook confirms that Tuesday lunch will be yam porridge and orange slices. Which menu entry tells pupils both the meal time and what they will receive?
options: Tuesday lunch — yam porridge and orange slices.
Tuesday — fruit will be served sometime.
Lunch — porridge, with the day to be announced.
Tuesday lunch — yam porridge and pineapple.
questions.answer: Tuesday lunch — yam porridge and orange slices.
questions.explanation: The entry includes the correct day, meal and both foods.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Select meals or menu descriptions that meet stated needs and constraints.
questions.prompt: A pupil is planning lunch for a small family. The family already has maize and beans, and can buy only one more item. Which choice adds a leafy vegetable without buying another staple?
options: A second bag of maize.
A bunch of amaranth leaves.
A loaf of bread.
A bag of rice.
questions.explanation: Amaranth leaves add the requested vegetable. The other choices add staples already represented in the meal.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify a kitchen hazard and select a practical way to reduce it.
questions.prompt: During a supervised cooking lesson, a pan handle sticks out over the edge of the stove into the walkway. What should the pupils ask the adult to do?
options: Place a plate under the handle.
Move the pan nearer to the edge.
Turn the handle away from the walkway and clear of other burners.
Keep the handle pointing out so it is easier to grab.
questions.answer: Turn the handle away from the walkway and clear of other burners.
questions.explanation: A handle in the walkway can be knocked, spilling hot food. Turning it away from traffic reduces that risk.

questions.subject: Quantitative and Vocational Aptitude
questions.learningObjective: Identify a kitchen hazard and select a practical way to reduce it.
questions.prompt: A bucket of water spills across the kitchen doorway during a school activity. What is the safest first response?
options: Carry on serving food while the floor dries.
Put a stool in the wet area and leave it unattended.
Walk through quickly to fetch dishes.
Warn people away and tell the supervising adult so the spill can be cleared.
questions.answer: Warn people away and tell the supervising adult so the spill can be cleared.
questions.explanation: Warning people and reporting the spill reduces the immediate slipping hazard.
